key_facts: UPDATED July 30 FINAL_DAY(T+1) after Thursday qualification at Scotstoun Stadium (final Friday July 31, 8:15 PM local / 19:15 GMT): Pathirage 0.40->0.45, Peters 0.19->0.22 (now #2), Chopra 0.22->0.18, Nadeem 0.06->0.05, Walcott 0.06->0.04 (sum=0.94; 6% outside top 5). Qualification occurred in cold (18C) and gusty/swirling 13 kmph headwinds/crosswinds; NO athlete breached 84m auto-Q, only 4 cleared 80m. Complete 12-man final: (1) Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage 82.84m on his SINGLE 1st throw (skipped 2nd/3rd! +1.55m clear of field; 2026 record: 89.28m Kip Keino 1st, 85.97m Rabat 2nd, 92.62m Rome DL 1st, 88.68m Doha DL 1st, 86.57m Ostrava 1st); (2) Anderson Peters 81.29m (2nd throw; 2026 Rabat DL winner, Rome 2nd, beat Chopra in Doha, 2025 Tokyo Worlds silver); (3) Douw Smit RSA 80.64m (1 throw); (4) Ben East ENG 80.38m; (5) Neeraj Chopra 79.61m (76.28m, 79.61m, skipped 3rd; wore skullcap struggling to stay warm, only 1 meet in 2026 after injury); (6) Cameron McEntyre AUS 78.91m; (7) Arshad Nadeem 78.63m (2nd sub-79m meet in 2026; told Al Jazeera cold Scottish weather hurts vs Pakistan heat and aimed for 'a podium finish'); (8) Keyshawn Strachan BAH 78.60m; (9) Rohit Yadav IND 78.37m (skipped 3rd, 87.05m PB); (10) Yash Vir Singh IND 78.36m; (11) Keshorn Walcott TTO 78.26m (reigning 2025 Tokyo World Champion barely snuck in at 11th); (12) Chinecherem Nnamdi NGR 75.27m. BIG SHOCK: Julius Yego (KEN) eliminated 13th (74.50m); Sumedha Ranasinghe NM. Gusty Scotstoun weather & 1-day javelin variance cap Pathirage at 0.45 despite clear technical & 2026 form superiority.
